questions.q: Is Northfield Outfitters, the company in this case study, a real business?
options: No — it is explicitly a fictional company invented to illustrate the concepts in this course
Yes — it is a real, named outdoor retailer
Yes, but its name has been changed for privacy
The lesson doesn't say either way
questions.explain: The guide states plainly that Northfield Outfitters is fictional and no statistic in the case study is a real industry figure.

questions.q: What pattern did profiling reveal that pointed to the root cause of the duplicate customer records?
options: The same person appeared as two near-identical rows, one from each source system, differing mainly in name formatting
All duplicate rows came from a single random data entry error
Every customer record was missing a phone number
The row count was lower than expected, not higher
questions.explain: That repeating two-systems-one-person shape is the signature of a missing cross-system identifier, not random error.

questions.q: Which three data quality dimensions, together, were involved in the Northfield Outfitters problem?
options: Uniqueness, consistency, and completeness
Timeliness, validity, and accuracy
Only uniqueness, with no other dimensions involved
Security, privacy, and availability
questions.explain: Uniqueness (duplicate rows), consistency (name formatting), and completeness (missing emails from POS) all appeared together.

questions.q: Why was rewriting the nightly load to upsert on a cross-system match key more important long-term than the one-time deduplication pass?
options: Without fixing the root cause, the load would keep appending new duplicate rows and the problem would return
Upserting is always faster to run than appending, regardless of correctness
The deduplication pass was unnecessary and could have been skipped
It had no real impact on preventing future duplicates
questions.explain: A fix that only cleans existing rows without addressing the cause would have worked for exactly one day, as the lesson states.

questions.q: What was put in place after the fix to keep the duplicate problem from silently recurring?
options: A monitor tracking the duplicate rate daily, surfaced on a scorecard
A one-time manual review scheduled for the following year
Nothing further was needed after the deduplication pass
A new uniqueness threshold that was never actually checked again
questions.explain: Following Lesson 26 and 27's pattern, ongoing monitoring plus a scorecard tile keeps the fix from quietly eroding over time.
